definitions.explanation: A popular Japanese dish of stir-fried wheat noodles with vegetables, meat, and a savory sauce. A staple of street food stalls at festivals and a common home-cooked meal.

examples.japanese: {昼|ひる}ごはん⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{焼|や}きそば⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
⟦{屋台|やたい}→屋台：10549_yatai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{焼|や}きそば⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ソース→ソース：17673_soosu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たまらない→たまらない：03409_tamaranai⟧。
examples.english: The aroma of sauce from the street stall yakisoba is irresistible.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{祭|まつ}り→お祭り：01349_omatsuri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}ったら→行く：00119_iku⟧、⟦まず→まず：00796_mazu⟧{焼|や}きそば⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦かき{氷|ごおり}→かき氷：10300_kakigoori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{定番|ていばん}→定番：12265_teiban⟧だ。
examples.english: When you go to a festival, buying yakisoba and shaved ice first is the standard routine.

notes:
USAGE:
Despite the name containing そば (buckwheat noodles), {焼|や}きそば is made with ⟦{中華|ちゅうか}{麺|めん}→中華麺：21814_chuukamen⟧ (Chinese-style wheat noodles), not buckwheat noodles. The noodles are stir-fried on a griddle with cabbage, pork, and other ingredients, then seasoned with a thick Worcestershire-type sauce.

FORMS:
- ⟦ソース→ソース：17673_soosu⟧{焼|や}きそば: the standard sauce-flavored version
- ⟦{塩|しお}→塩：00887_shio⟧{焼|や}きそば: salt-flavored yakisoba
- {焼|や}きそば⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧: a bread roll filled with yakisoba, popular at convenience stores and school cafeterias

CULTURAL NOTE:
{焼|や}きそば is closely associated with ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧ (festivals) and ⟦{屋台|やたい}→屋台：10549_yatai⟧ (food stalls). It is one of the most iconic ⟦{屋台|やたい}→屋台：10549_yatai⟧ foods alongside ⟦たこ{焼|や}き→たこ焼き：10364_takoyaki⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼|や}きそば⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make yakisoba
- {焼|や}きそば⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧: to cook yakisoba
- ⟦{屋台|やたい}→屋台：10549_yatai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{焼|や}きそば: festival stall yakisoba
